problemStatement.formal:
Let $\omega(n)$ count the number of distinct primes dividing $n$. Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $m<n$, we have $m+\omega(m) \leq n$?

Can one show that there exists an $\epsilon>0$ such that there are infinitely many $n$ where $m+\epsilon \omega(m)\leq n$ for all $m<n$?
problemStatement.plain: Are there infinitely many barriers for ω (number of distinct prime divisors)?
whyMatters: Connects to iterated dynamics of n → n + ω(n)

proven: ω-barriers verified by native_decide up to 720 (OEIS A005236)
φ has no barriers beyond 3 (proved: φ(n-1) ≥ 2 for n ≥ 4)
σ₁ has no barriers beyond 2 (proved: σ₁(n) ≥ n+1 for n ≥ 2)
Barrier predecessor characterization: at barrier n ≥ 2, n-1 is 1 or prime power
Consecutive barriers require prime power: n, n+1 both barriers ⟹ ω(n) ≤ 1
Barrier hierarchy verified: F-barriers >> ω-barriers >> Ω-barriers
Ω-barriers verified: only 4 up to 5 (very rare)
Barrier trapping: orbit from m < b stays ≤ b after one step
open: Main conjecture: ω has infinitely many barriers
Epsilon variant: ∃ ε > 0 with infinitely many ε-barriers
All trajectories of n → n + ω(n) eventually meet

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: 1104-line formalization with 122 proved theorems, 0 sorries, 6 axioms (all genuinely open). Includes omega coprime multiplicativity, subadditivity, strong predecessor characterization, barrier offset bounds, squarefree equivalence, phi/sigma non-barrier proofs, and verified barrier hierarchy F >> ω >> Ω.
builtItems: Euler totient no-barriers theorem (proved, not axiom)
omega_mul_coprime: ω(mn) = ω(m) + ω(n) for coprime m,n (proved)
barrier_offset_bound: at barrier n, ω(n-j) ≤ j (proved)
insights: Barriers for ω are exactly those n where all m < n satisfy m + ω(m) ≤ n
At any barrier n ≥ 2, n-1 must be 1 or a prime power (ω(n-1) ≤ 1)
φ and σ grow too fast for barriers: φ(n) ≥ 2 for n ≥ 3, σ(n) ≥ n+1 for n ≥ 2
F = ∏kᵢ has ~65% density of barriers (verified up to 100)
ω-barriers get sparser: 26 up to 721, density ~3.6%
Ω-barriers are extremely rare: only 4 up to 5
The barrier hierarchy F >> ω >> Ω reflects growth rate ordering
native_decide with attribute [-instance] Classical.propDecidable enables computable proofs
Orbit dynamics: iteration n → n + ω(n) is strictly increasing for n ≥ 2
